topic: Neptune has the fastest winds in the solar system
claim: Neptune's winds top 1,200 mph (2,000 km/h), the fastest in the solar system, even though the planet gets very little energy from the Sun.

beats.caption: Fastest winds in space
beats.vo: Neptune has the fastest winds in the solar system.

beats.caption: 30x farther than Earth
beats.vo: It's over thirty times farther from the Sun than Earth, so it gets very little energy.

beats.caption: Wind speed, mph
beats.vo: Yet its winds top twelve hundred miles per hour. Earth's strongest winds only reach about two hundred fifty.

beats.caption: 3x Jupiter's winds
beats.vo: That's up to three times faster than the winds on Jupiter.

beats.caption: Voyager 2, 1989
beats.vo: Voyager 2 flew past in nineteen eighty-nine, the first spacecraft ever to visit. It spotted a storm big enough to swallow Earth whole.

beats.caption: Where does the power come from?
beats.vo: Dim sunlight, deep cold, and still the windiest world we know. So what's powering it?

sources.text: NASA Science, Neptune Facts: https://science.nasa.gov/neptune/neptune-facts/ (winds >1,200 mph / 2,000 km/h; Earth's strongest ~250 mph / 400 km/h; >30x Earth's distance from the Sun; Voyager 2 first flyby 1989; Great Dark Spot large enough to contain Earth)
